After her debut book, _Conversations with Friends_ , was published in 2017,
Irish novelist Sally Rooney gave an interview in which she spoke about the
novel's themes of class, interpersonal power, and privilege. "People,
particularly older wealthy people," she said, "do not take the radical views
of young women seriously."

Since that prescient interview, much has changed. Rooney sold millions of
books, adapted two of her novels into wildly popular mini-series, and made
sure the radical views of young women, such as herself, were not just taken
seriously but were bona fide and impossible to ignore. The author denounced
Israel's genocide in Gaza, was [vocal in her
support](https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-interactive/2026/may/19/sally-
rooney-new-hebrew-translation-intermezzo?utm_source=chatgpt.com) for the
Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement,
[refused](https://www.972mag.com/sally-rooney-hebrew-translation-israel-bds-
intermezzo/) to publish her latest two books in Hebrew with an Israeli
publisher tied to the military, and pledged her support for Palestine Action
by [donating](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/16/nx-s1-6004838/sally-rooney-books-
uk-palestinian-action-support) the royalties from her work to the proscribed
group (The UK [proscribed](https://zeteo.com/p/uk-bans-palestine-action-as-
terror) the group as a terrorist organization in 2025 and the U.S.
[followed](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/26/us-issues-
sanctions-uk-based-palestine-action) with the label and sanctions this year).

Let us be clear: Palestine Action, whose stated aims are to stop Israeli war
crimes and British complicity in them by disrupting the production of weapons,
mainly Elbit Systems, Israel's largest arms company, is not a terrorist group.
It was the government of Keir 'Israel has a legal right to cut water and
electricity to Palestinians' Starmer, laughably, a former human rights lawyer,
that proscribed it under the UK Terrorism Act 2000, placing it on the same
footing as al-Qaeda. By pledging her earnings to Palestine Action, Rooney
placed herself at risk of arrest if she enters the UK. Now, her publishers
can't pay her for her work, and she's been forced to
[withdraw](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/14/sally-rooney-says-
she-can-no-longer-sell-books-in-the-uk-because-of-palestine-action-support)
all her books from sale in the UK. It is an extraordinary act of Orwellian
villainy, censorship, and oppression by the UK. If they can shut down one of
the most popular writers of her time, what other line won't they cross?
